verdict.rationale: Clerk is fundamentally an auth/user-management platform, not a workflow/automation engine, but its 'eve' AI-agent features (M2M tokens for agent-to-agent auth, tool-call permission gating, OAuth brokering) and webhooks provide the identity/authorization backbone that could let autonomous agents act in the background under scoped credentials. There is no evidence of an actual scheduling/orchestration/automation-builder capability that runs tasks autonomously — only the auth primitives an agent would need. Missing for 10: evidence of an actual automation/workflow execution engine, scheduling or triggers beyond webhooks, and any documented autonomous background job running natively in Clerk.
